prerequisites: All compulsory and elective subjects of the Master's must be completed and approved, with the exception of the TFM itself.

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context (CB6).

Students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study (CB7).

Students are able to integrate knowledge and deal with the complexity of formulating judgments based on incomplete or limited information, including reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments (CB8).
Students know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way (CB9).
Students possess learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that will be largely self-directed or autonomous (CB10).
Develop problem-solving skills in new or little-known environments within multidisciplinary contexts related to energy engineering (CG1).
Achieve the ability to integrate knowledge to formulate applications for the development of new energy technologies (CG2).

Acquire autonomous learning skills that allow for continued study through the development of the ability to search for specialized documentation in cutting-edge scientific-technical literature and its assimilation (CG3).
Application of experimentation techniques for measuring variables and testing operational performance of machines and equipment (CE1).
Design, planning, and development of simple experiments for studies on fluid flows and energy transfer (CE2).
Acquisition, processing, and analysis of signals in time and frequency domains (CE3).
Application of computational analysis methodologies for numerical modeling of fluid flows and energy transfers of interest (CE6).
Fundamental analysis of fluid mechanical and thermal problems of interest in the energy industry, identifying strong and weak variables and evaluating possible simplifying hypotheses (CE7).
Performance of elementary calculations for sizing, selection of machines and equipment, and operation for installations with fluids with energy transfers (CE8).

Ability to study, propose, and apply different types of technologies to improve the utilization and energy efficiency of installations or plants, comparing alternatives by performance and costs (CE9).
Knowledge of advances and latest trends in general equipment and operating characteristics of hydraulic and wind power plants (CE10).
Ability for thermodynamic and economic analysis of installations and their elements, for the evaluation of energy efficiency (CE11).
Evaluation and application of advanced technologies for thermoelectric generation with minimum pollutant emissions (CE12).

Understand the basic process of carrying out a work, which includes choosing it, bibliographic study, work planning, exposition of options, study of each of them, selection of the most convenient, development of it, and conclusions.
Manage documentation search tools to establish the state of the art and subsequent presentation of it.
Establish different options for carrying out a work of these characteristics.
Plan a work plan for the study of different options.
Evaluate the results obtained from the study of the different possible options in order to choose the most appropriate one.
Carry out the final development of the chosen option.
Correctly establish the final conclusions taking into account the entirety of the work carried out.

syllabus_topics: Application of knowledge and techniques of Energy Engineering to a project, memoir, or study.
Problem-solving or research proposed and agreed between the student and the tutor/s.

assessment_methods.method: Public defense of the Master's Thesis before an examining board

assessment_rules: The evaluation is carried out by the grade awarded by the examining board during the public defense of the work, which must be a numerical score. The student can defend their TFM once all the credits of the degree have been passed, except those corresponding to the TFM itself. The final grade will be given by the examining board at the defense of the work. If sanitary conditions require it, non-face-to-face evaluation methods may be included, and students will be informed of any changes.
institution: Universidad de Oviedo - Máster Universitario en Ingeniería Energética (EPI Gijón)
